coul14_rules.comment: TraPPE's glycol ethers, diols, disulfides and (meth)acrylates count 1-4 Coulomb x 0.5; so does any chain with two O three carbons apart (Stubbs et al. 2004: 1-4 charge pairs x 1/2, e.g. poly(vinyl alcohol), poly(vinyl ethers))

virtual_sites.comment: N2's centre charge, midway between the atoms
O2's centre charge, midway between the atoms
NH3's charge on the axis, 0.08 A from N towards the H
H2S's charge on the bisector, 0.3 A from S

notes: built by CAPS (bench/ff/make_trappe.py) from the TraPPE database's own models (trappe.oit.umn.edu), each term with its paper

rigid models (ammonia, benzene (6 site), carbon dioxide, ethylene oxide, m-xylene, naphthalene, nitrogen, o-xylene, oxygen, p-xylene, thiophene, toluene (7 site)) have no intramolecular terms in TraPPE: their angles are stiff here; hold them rigid

1-4 Coulomb x 0.5 in TraPPE for 1,2-dimethoxyethane, 1,2-ethanediol, 1,3-propanediol, 2-ethylhexyl acrylate, 2-hydroxyethyl acrylate, 2-methoxyethan-1-ol, diethyl disulfide, dimethyl disulfide, ethyl acrylate, ethyl methacrylate, methyl acrylate, methyl methacrylate, n-butyl acrylate, n-butyl methacrylate, n-octyl acrylate (coul14_rules); every other 1-4 pair excluded
TraPPE fixes bond lengths: bonds are stiff harmonic (600 kcal/mol/A^2), to be constrained in MD

transferable hydrocarbon terms (bonds, bends, torsions by pseudo-atom kind) from M.G. Martin, J.I. Siepmann, J. Phys. Chem. B 102, 2569 (1998), M.G. Martin, J.I. Siepmann, J. Phys. Chem. B 103, 4508 (1999) Table 2 and C.D. Wick, M.G. Martin, J.I. Siepmann, J. Phys. Chem. B 104, 8008 (2000) Tables 2-4, written over CH3_2 CH2_3 CH_4 C_5 (sp3), CH2_29 CH_30 C_31 (sp2) and CH_88 C_89 (aromatic); a term a database model gives comes later in each list and wins; where both give one they agree

M.G. Martin, J.I. Siepmann, J. Phys. Chem. B 103, 4508 (1999) Table 2 prints c1 335.03 K for CHx-(CH2)-(CH2)-CHy; M.G. Martin, J.I. Siepmann, J. Phys. Chem. B 102, 2569 (1998) (eq 5), C.D. Wick, M.G. Martin, J.I. Siepmann, J. Phys. Chem. B 104, 8008 (2000) Table 4 and the database give 355.03 K, used here

C.D. Wick, M.G. Martin, J.I. Siepmann, J. Phys. Chem. B 104, 8008 (2000) Table 4 prints d0 12400 K (cis) and 13400 K (trans) for d0 / 2 (phi - phi0)^2 about CHx-CH=CH-CHy; the database's cis- and trans-2-butene give 24800 and 26800 K; both the 2-butenes and the transferable term use the database's values

C.D. Wick, M.G. Martin, J.I. Siepmann, J. Phys. Chem. B 104, 8008 (2000) Table 4 names the second aromatic torsion CHx(aro)-C(aro)-CH(sp2)-CHx; the database uses it for isopropylbenzene's sp3 CH, and so does CAPS (CH_4)

transferable alcohol, ether and glycol terms from B. Chen, J.J. Potoff, J.I. Siepmann, J. Phys. Chem. B 105, 3093 (2001) Table 1 and J.M. Stubbs, J.J. Potoff, J.I. Siepmann, J. Phys. Chem. B 108, 17596 (2004) Table 1 over the hydroxyl and ether O, H and the carbons bonded to them (CH3_8 CH2_9 CH_10 C_11, CH3_16 CH2_17 CH_18 C_19); 1-4 Coulomb x 0.5 as the 2004 paper counts it for any chain with two O three carbons apart (poly(vinyl alcohol), poly(vinyl ethers))

readings: a C-C torsion of the 1999 Table 2 (CHx-CH2-CH-CHy, CHx-CH-CH-CHy, CHx-CH2-C-CHy) with one O end takes the carbon term, as the database's 2-butanol does; O-CH2-CH-O, O-C-O-C and every acetal term are in none of the tables
CHx-(CH)-(O)-H: B. Chen, J.J. Potoff, J.I. Siepmann, J. Phys. Chem. B 105, 3093 (2001) Table 1 prints c0 215.96 K, the database's propan-2-ol and 2-butanol 215.89 K (a constant); 215.89 used

five- and six-membered cycloalkane rings (S.J. Keasler, S.M. Charan, C.D. Wick, I.G. Economou, J.I. Siepmann, J. Phys. Chem. B 116, 11234 (2012) Tables 2 and 3) over CH2_141 / CH2_140 and a ring CH or C carrying a substituent (typed CH_4 / C_5, linear Lennard-Jones: the paper fits CH2 rings only); a bend or torsion with an end outside the ring takes the linear term; carbons shared by two rings (fused, bridged) stay untyped

the 2012 paper's torsions (the database's C3 form, every five- and six-membered ring model) are a series in psi = phi - 180: their minima are the rings' own torsions (cyclohexane chair 55 deg: c0 - c1 cos + ... = 12 K), where read in phi they put 15 kcal/mol into every cyclohexane torsion; before this the library read them in phi
